title: Default Global Test
description: Standard marking and global timing test.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Gold?
questions.subject: Science
questions.explanation: Au is derived from the Latin word 'Aurum'.

questions.question: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.subject: Science
questions.explanation: The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

questions.question: Which of these are noble gases?
questions.subject: Science
questions.explanation: Noble gases are inert gases like Neon, Argon, Xenon, etc.

questions.question: In what year did World War II end?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: WWII ended in 1945 with the surrender of Japan.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: George Washington served from 1789 to 1797.

questions.question: Which countries were members of the Axis powers?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: The main Axis powers were Germany, Italy, and Japan.

questions.question: What is 12 multiplied by 12?
questions.subject: Math

questions.question: Which of these are prime numbers less than 10?
questions.subject: Math
questions.explanation: Prime numbers have only two divisors: 1 and themselves.

questions.question: What does RAM stand for?
questions.subject: Tech
questions.explanation: RAM is the short-term memory of a computer.

questions.question: In what year was the Java programming language first released?
questions.subject: Tech
questions.explanation: Java was released by Sun Microsystems in 1995.

questions.question: Which of these are major cloud computing providers?
questions.subject: Tech
questions.explanation: All four are prominent cloud infrastructure providers.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.

questions.question: Which of these are Great Lakes of North America?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The five Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario.

questions.question: How many continents are there on Earth?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.subject: Literature
questions.explanation: Shakespeare wrote this famous tragedy early in his career.

questions.question: Which of these are Hogwarts houses in Harry Potter?
questions.subject: Literature
questions.explanation: The four houses are Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw, and Slytherin.

questions.question: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.subject: Biology
questions.explanation: Adults typically have 206 bones.

questions.question: What is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.subject: Biology
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the cell's supply of ATP.

questions.question: Which of these are the four nucleobases in DNA?
questions.subject: Biology
questions.explanation: DNA contains A, T, C, G. RNA contains Uracil instead of Thymine.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in meters per second?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.explanation: The speed of light is roughly 299,792,458 m/s.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.explanation: Force is measured in Newtons (kg m/s^2).

questions.question: What are the four fundamental forces of nature?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.explanation: The four fundamental interactions are gravity, electromagnetism, and the strong and weak nuclear forces.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of Carbon?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.explanation: Carbon is the 6th element in the periodic table.

questions.question: What is the pH of pure water?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral with a pH of 7.

questions.question: Which of these are halogens?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.explanation: Halogens are elements in Group 17 of the periodic table.
